summary: Daniel B. Stevenson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He held posts as an assistant professor at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003), and was a guest scholar at Soka University.

Daniel Baum is a linguist and Indologist. He earned a BA at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1992–1996), studied under Saul Migron, and completed his doctorate at Leiden University (1997–2005) under Alexander Lubotsky.
Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at Indiana University Bloomington and the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D. completed by 1996 under Victor H. Mair, Gregory Schopen, and Ludo Rocher), he has served as an associate professor at Cornell University.

Daniel Clarke Waugh is a historian of Central Asia and Iran. He earned a B.A. from Yale University in 1963 and master's and doctoral degrees from Harvard University (1965, 1972) before joining the faculty at the University of Washington in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as librarian at Yale (1856–1872), president of the University of California (1872–1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution (1902–1904).

Daniel Cozort is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (~1980–1989) under Jeffrey Hopkins and several traditional teachers, later teaching at Bates College (~1987–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988).

Daniel Dubuisson is a scholar in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts as director of research at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III and the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2010).

Daniel Franz Schauffelberger was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1838–1841), Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1841–1843), and the University of Bonn (~1843–1845), where he earned his Ph.D.

Daniel H. H. Ingalls was an Indologist and philosopher. He earned his A.B. and A.M. at Harvard University, studying under Walter Eugene Clark and Kalipada Tarkacharya, and served on the Harvard faculty from 1938 to 1983 as an assistant professor.

Daniel John Gogerly was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He headed the Wesleyan Mission Press (~1818), served as General Superintendent of the Wesleyan Mission in South Ceylon (1838), and was secretary, vice-president, and president of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka (~1845–1858).

Daniel L. Overmyer was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned his master's and doctorate at the University of Chicago under Philip A. Kuhn. He was a professor at the University of British Columbia (~1973–2001) and held multiple visiting posts.

Daniel M. Neuman is an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1974. He held academic posts at Dartmouth College (1971–1980), the University of Washington (1980–1995), and the University of California, Los Angeles (1995–2018).

Daniel M. Stuart is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley (attested 2012) under Alexander von Rospatt and served as an assistant professor at the University of South Carolina (attested 2017) and visiting professor at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Daniel P. Brown was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Geshe Wangyal. He served as a professor at Harvard University.

Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his graduate thesis research at Florida State University under the supervision of Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Schlumberger was a historian and archaeologist of Central Asia and Iran. He studied at Strasbourg and Paris (Ph.D. ~1950), served as an inspector for antiquities in the Levant (1929–1940), and became Professor of Byzantine and Near Eastern History at Strasbourg in 1955.

Daniel Sperber is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London (~1965–1968) and held academic posts at Bar-Ilan University (~1968) and the Open University of Israel.

Daniel Stuart Capper specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from the University of Virginia (-1987) and a Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (-2000), later serving as professor at the University of Southern Mississippi (2000–2022) and Metropolitan State University of Denver (2023).

Daniel Timothy Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania, having studied under Parimal G. Patil, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.
